subject.title: [Google Antigravity Ban] Frequent Tool Schema Reloading Causes False Positive Anti-Abuse Detection

question: Should OpenClaw land a bounded internal cache for provider-normalized tool schema parameters on the embedded attempt path, and what invalidation boundary should it use?
rationale: The repeated-normalization path is clear, but the permanent cache boundary affects provider hooks, plugin metadata lifecycle, custom provider behavior, and the prepared-runtime migration direction.

options.title: Land a narrow internal cache
options.body: Refresh or replace the open cache PR with the bounded shape that caches cloned schema parameters only for known safe provider hooks while rebuilding tool objects and closures per turn.

options.title: Defer to prepared-runtime migration
options.body: Keep this issue open until the broader prepared-runtime rollout carries enough provider/tool facts to remove the need for a separate cache layer.

options.title: Require live proof first
options.body: Hold implementation until a maintainer or reporter captures current-main live Google/Gemini or heap evidence showing the user-visible impact still occurs.

recommendation.title: Land a narrow internal cache
recommendation.body: Refresh or replace the open cache PR with the bounded shape that caches cloned schema parameters only for known safe provider hooks while rebuilding tool objects and closures per turn.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision intersects the prepared-runtime migration boundary and the broader request-time rediscovery tracker.
